source_url: Hand-built from verified public histories; per-feature source URL in each feature's source property. Synthesis: dataset-synthesis-2026-11-20.md §5.7-5.8. Community list: http://mn.gov/indian-affairs/tribal-nations-in-minnesota/gaa-zagaskwaajimekaag-leech-lake-band-of-ojibwe.jsp
query: No service query — hand-built point layer. Point-in-polygon clip test against scripts/huc8-07010102-clip.geojson (WBD HUC8 07010102) run 2026-11-21; GNIS populated-place status checked where available (geocoder + GNIS-derived coordinates via TopoQuest/NYBG/Wikipedia GNIS citations).
caveats: Hand-placed points; location_precision is 'approximate' for every feature — community centers, not surveyed sites. CLIP OUTCOME: 8 in-watershed (Walker, Federal Dam, Boy River, Onigum, Bena, Sugar Point, Oak Point, Smokey Point); 6 labeled neighbors outside HUC8 07010102 (Cass Lake, Ball Club, Inger, Squaw Lake, Mission, Pennington). Cass Lake confirms synthesis §4.4 (city polygon 0-intersects the watershed). Bena is IN the watershed by the clip, contrary to the earlier 'likely outside HUC' expectation — corroborated by synthesis §4.4, which lists Bena among the 9 incorporated places intersecting the watershed. Ball Club (~2.7 km), Pennington (~7.4 km), Mission (~9.3 km), Inger (~24 km) and Squaw Lake (~29 km) lie outside the HUC8 boundary but are Reservation communities, kept as labeled neighbors. Founding dates are null wherever not verified: all eight Reservation communities (Ball Club, Inger, Squaw Lake, Sugar Point, Oak Point, Mission, Pennington, Smokey Point) plus Onigum and Bena carry no invented date — founding histories need Band sources. Steamboat Bay is NOT listed: it is a bay (starry-stonewort/Anderson's Cove site), not a verified settlement. Whipholt is NOT listed as a feature: named community near Walker with no verified founding date — recorded here as a gap. Mission and Sugar Point/Oak Point/Smokey Point placements are the least certain (cemetery/road/cape anchors, flagged in each feature's notes) and need Band confirmation. THPO/Band: YES for any historical characterization of Onigum and the Reservation communities — this layer carries factual names only, no characterization. Dates are from histories, not GNIS.
